claim: Odorant binding proteins (Obps) are expressed at extremely high levels in the antennae of insects.
source: Odorant binding proteins (Obps) are expressed at extremely high levels in the antennae of insects, and have long been believed essential for carrying hydrophobic odorants to odor receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about Obp expression levels.

claim: Obps have long been believed essential for carrying hydrophobic odorants to odor receptors.
source: Odorant binding proteins (Obps) are expressed at extremely high levels in the antennae of insects, and have long been believed essential for carrying hydrophobic odorants to odor receptors.
evidence: This describes the historical scientific belief about Obp function.

claim: When one functional type of olfactory sensillum in Drosophila was depleted of its sole abundant Obp, it retained a robust olfactory response.
source: Previously we found that when one functional type of olfactory sensillum in Drosophila was depleted of its sole abundant Obp, it retained a robust olfactory response (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: All of six tested sensillum types responded robustly to odors of widely diverse chemical or temporal structure when all abundant Obp genes in antennal basiconic sensilla were deleted.
source: Here we have deleted all the Obp genes that are abundantly expressed in the antennal basiconic sensilla. All of six tested sensillum types responded robustly to odors of widely diverse chemical or temporal structure.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: One mutant gave a greater physiological and behavioral response to an odorant that affects oviposition.
source: One mutant gave a greater physiological and behavioral response to an odorant that affects oviposition.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: Many sensilla can respond to odorants in the absence of Obps.
source: Our results support a model in which many sensilla can respond to odorants in the absence of Obps, and many Obps are not essential for olfactory response, but that some Obps can modulate olfactory physiology and the behavior that it drives.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Many Obps are not essential for olfactory response.
source: Our results support a model in which many sensilla can respond to odorants in the absence of Obps, and many Obps are not essential for olfactory response, but that some Obps can modulate olfactory physiology and the behavior that it drives.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Some Obps can modulate olfactory physiology and the behavior that it drives.
source: Our results support a model in which many sensilla can respond to odorants in the absence of Obps, and many Obps are not essential for olfactory response, but that some Obps can modulate olfactory physiology and the behavior that it drives.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data, particularly the linoleic acid results.

claim: The Drosophila antenna detects an enormous variety of odorants via olfactory sensilla on the antennal surface.
source: The Drosophila antenna detects an enormous variety of odorants via olfactory sensilla on the antennal surface (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila olfaction, supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: The basiconic sensilla are sensitive to many fruit odors.
source: One morphological class of sensilla, the basiconic sensilla, is sensitive to many fruit odors (de Bruyne et al., 2001; Dweck et al., 2018; Hallem and Carlson, 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: There are 10 functionally distinct types of antennal basiconic (ab) sensilla, termed ab1-ab10.
source: There are 10 functionally distinct types of antennal basiconic (ab) sensilla, termed ab1-ab10 (Couto et al., 2005; de Bruyne et al., 2001; Grabe et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila olfactory system organization, supported by citations.

claim: Each basiconic sensillum contains pores through which odorants can pass.
source: Each of these sensilla contains pores through which odorants can pass, and each contains the dendrites of two or four olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) immersed in an aqueous lymph (Figure 1D) (Shanbhag et al., 1999; Shanbhag et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge about sensillum structure, supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: Each basiconic sensillum contains the dendrites of two or four olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) immersed in an aqueous lymph.
source: Each of these sensilla contains pores through which odorants can pass, and each contains the dendrites of two or four olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) immersed in an aqueous lymph (Figure 1D) (Shanbhag et al., 1999; Shanbhag et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge about sensillum structure, supported by citations and illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: The ORNs within a sensillum are distinguishable based on their spike amplitudes and response spectra.
source: The ORNs within a sensillum are distinguishable based on their spike amplitudes and response spectra, and are designated by letters, for example the ab2 sensillum contains ORNs ab2A and ab2B.
evidence: This describes established methodology for identifying ORNs.

claim: Two major classes of molecules are believed essential to olfactory detection, discrimination, and behavior: odor receptors and odorant binding proteins (Obps).
source: Two major classes of molecules are believed essential to this process, odor receptors and odorant binding proteins (Obps) (Leal, 2013).
evidence: This describes the prevailing scientific view, supported by citation.

claim: The in vivo functions of many odorant receptors have been well established.
source: The in vivo functions of many odorant receptors have been well established (Ai et al., 2010; Benton et al., 2009; Ha and Smith, 2006; Hallem and Carlson, 2006; Hallem et al., 2004; van der Goes van Naters and Carlson, 2007; Yao et al., 2005)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: A cryo-EM structure for an odor receptor co-receptor, Orco, was recently determined.
source: but their structures are only now beginning to be solved, with the recent determination of a cryo-EM structure for an odor receptor co-receptor, Orco (Butterwick et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a recent finding from another study, supported by citation.

claim: The structures of many Obps have been solved at high resolution.
source: Reciprocally, the structures of many Obps have been solved at high resolution (Brito et al., 2016; Kruse et al., 2003; Laughlin et al., 2008; Leite et al., 2009; Sandler et al., 2000)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The functions of Obps in vivo are much less clear than their structures.
source: Reciprocally, the structures of many Obps have been solved at high resolution (Brito et al., 2016; Kruse et al., 2003; Laughlin et al., 2008; Leite et al., 2009; Sandler et al., 2000), but their functions in vivo are much less clear (Bentzur et al., 2018; Gomez-Diaz et al., 2013; Kim et al., 1998; Larter et al., 2016; Sun et al., 2018b; Xu et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an assessment of the state of knowledge, supported by citations.

claim: Obp mRNAs are the most abundant in the Drosophila antenna.
source: They are extraordinarily abundant, with Obp mRNAs being the most abundant in the Drosophila antenna (Menuz et al., 2014; Vogt et al., 1989).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: There are 52 Obp genes in Drosophila melanogaster.
source: There are a great number of them, for example there are 52 Obp genes in Drosophila melanogaster (Vieira and Rozas, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Obps are widely divergent in sequence.
source: Obps are widely divergent in sequence (Hekmat-Scafe et al., 2002), suggesting they may be divergent in function.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Obps may be divergent in function.
source: Obps are widely divergent in sequence (Hekmat-Scafe et al., 2002), suggesting they may be divergent in function.
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence divergence.

claim: The overall structure of Obps is conserved despite their variable sequence.
source: Despite their variable sequence, their overall structure is conserved.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Obp structure.

claim: Obps are small proteins on the order of 14 kDa.
source: Obps are small proteins on the order of 14 kDa, with six conserved cysteines that form three disulfide bridges linking six α-helices (Graham and Davies, 2002; Leal et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Obp structure, supported by citations.

claim: Obps have six conserved cysteines that form three disulfide bridges linking six α-helices.
source: Obps are small proteins on the order of 14 kDa, with six conserved cysteines that form three disulfide bridges linking six α-helices (Graham and Davies, 2002; Leal et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Obp structure, supported by citations.

claim: Many Obps bind odorants in vitro.
source: In vitro, many Obps bind odorants. The binding characteristics of Obps from widely diverse insects have been described in detail (Brito et al., 2016; Leal, 2013; Leal et al., 2005; Ziegelberger, 1995).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Many Obps are found in the aqueous lymph of the olfactory sensilla.
source: Many Obps are found in the aqueous lymph of the olfactory sensilla (Klein, 1987; Shanbhag et al., 2005; Vogt and Riddiford, 1981).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Obps provide an efficient solution for the transport of hydrophobic odorants through the aqueous sensillar lymph according to a widely accepted model.
source: Their odor-binding properties, location, and abundance have led to a model in which they provide an efficient solution to a difficult problem: the transport of hydrophobic odorants through the aqueous sensillar lymph (Kaissling, 2009; Klein et al., 1987; Leal, 2013; van den Berg and Ziegelberger, 1991; Vogt, 1991; Zhou et al., 2004). This model has been widely accepted for more than 30 years.
evidence: This describes a prevailing model in the field, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The distribution of Obps in the antenna had not been determined comprehensively at high resolution in Drosophila or any other insect prior to the authors' work.
source: A major barrier to studying the in vivo function of Obps has been that their distribution in the antenna had not been determined comprehensively at high resolution, in Drosophila or in any other insect.
evidence: This describes the state of the field before the authors' work.

claim: The authors constructed an Obp-to-sensillum map of the abundant antennal Obps.
source: We recently overcame this barrier by constructing an Obp-to-sensillum map of the abundant antennal Obps, that is 10 Obps whose RNAs were expressed at much higher levels than all others in the antenna (Figure 1E) (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors, supported by citation and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: 10 Obps have RNAs expressed at much higher levels than all others in the antenna.
source: We recently overcame this barrier by constructing an Obp-to-sensillum map of the abundant antennal Obps, that is 10 Obps whose RNAs were expressed at much higher levels than all others in the antenna (Figure 1E) (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The Obp-to-sensillum map was established via double-label experiments using Obp in situ hybridization probes and well-defined Or-GAL4 drivers.
source: The map was established via double-label experiments using Obp in situ hybridization probes and well-defined Or-GAL4 drivers that label particular sensillum types.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the authors' previous work.

claim: The ab8 sensillum contained a single abundant Obp, Obp28a.
source: The map revealed that one type of sensillum, ab8, contained a single abundant Obp, Obp28a (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The ab8 sensillum retained robust olfactory responses when the Obp28a gene was deleted.
source: We deleted the Obp28a gene and were startled to find that the ab8 sensillum retained robust olfactory responses.
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work.

claim: Responses to odor pulses in ab8 were either normal or of somewhat greater magnitude when Obp28a was deleted.
source: We tested a wide variety of odorants and found that responses to odor pulses were either normal or, in some cases, of somewhat greater magnitude.
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work.

claim: Obp28a is not essential in ab8 for robust olfactory response to a wide variety of compounds.
source: These data indicated that Obp28a is not essential in ab8 for robust olfactory response to a wide variety of compounds, and that the ab8 sensillum does not require its sole abundant Obp in order to respond robustly.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the authors' previous work.

claim: The ab8 sensillum does not require its sole abundant Obp in order to respond robustly.
source: These data indicated that Obp28a is not essential in ab8 for robust olfactory response to a wide variety of compounds, and that the ab8 sensillum does not require its sole abundant Obp in order to respond robustly.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the authors' previous work.

claim: Obp28a is the only Obp that is expressed in all basiconic sensilla.
source: Obp28a is the only Obp that is expressed in all basiconic sensilla, suggesting that its function might not be representative of other Obps.
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work, illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: All deletions were outcrossed for five generations to a control genotype, Canton-S w1118, to minimize genetic background effects.
source: All of the deletions were outcrossed for five generations to a control genotype, Canton-S w1118, in order to minimize genetic background effects.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: The absence of the deleted DNA was verified by PCR analysis at least three times.
source: The absence of the deleted DNA was verified by PCR analysis at least three times: after construction of the original deletions, after backcrossing to Canton-S w1118, and after recombining the mutations together.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: No gross defects in size, morphology, or position were detected in mutant sensilla lacking all four Obps.
source: On the order of 1000 basiconic sensilla were examined from the antennae of ~20 mutant flies lacking all four Obps. No gross defects in size, morphology, or position were detected (Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 1B,C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: ab1 sensilla lacking their three abundant Obps showed strong responses to ethyl acetate.
source: ab1 sensilla lacking their three abundant Obps showed strong responses to ethyl acetate, which activates the ab1A neuron (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: Response magnitudes of the ab1 mutant were indistinguishable from those of the genetic background control for ethyl acetate at two concentrations.
source: Response magnitudes of the mutant were indistinguishable from those of the genetic background control, at each of two concentrations.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: ab1 responses to 2,3-butanedione were normal when three Obps were removed genetically.
source: Responses were also normal when tested with two concentrations of 2,3-butanedione, which activates the ab1B neuron (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2A.

claim: ab2 sensilla showed normal responses of both A and B neurons when three Obps were removed genetically.
source: ab2 sensilla likewise showed normal responses of both A and B neurons when these three Obps were removed genetically (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2B.

claim: ab3 sensilla showed normal responses of both ab3A and ab3B neurons following removal of all four of their abundant Obps.
source: ab3 sensilla were tested following removal of all four of their abundant Obps. Responses of both ab3A and ab3B neurons to the test odorants were normal, compared to the genetic background control (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2C.

claim: ab4, ab5, and ab6 showed normal responses to A and B neurons in Obp19a; Obp28a double mutants.
source: ab4, ab5, and ab6 were tested in Obp19a; Obp28a double mutants. Responses to A and B neurons were normal in each of the three sensillum types (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2D-F.

claim: Geosmin and geranyl acetate are both highly hydrophobic.
source: We note that geosmin and geranyl acetate, which elicited normal responses, are both highly hydrophobic (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 showing logP values.

claim: 73 additional odorant-ORN combinations all showed normal responses to a 0.5 s pulse of odorant in either the initial screen or rescreen.
source: To determine whether we could identify an olfactory response that was affected by the loss of Obps, we screened an additional 73 odorant-ORN combinations. These odorants included two that are more hydrophobic than any in the original set: geranyl acetone (logP = 4.13) and citronellyl acetate (logP = 4.28). All showed normal responses to a 0.5 s pulse of odorant in either the initial screen at a low n value (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–D) or, in the case of 3 of the 73 odorants, in a rescreen at a higher n value (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E; the rescreen also included five control odorants).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The spontaneous activity level of all 12 neurons was normal in the absence of abundant Obps.
source: We note finally that the spontaneous activity level of all 12 neurons was normal in the absence of abundant Obps (p>0.05 in all cases, Mann-Whitney U test, n = 10).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by statistical analysis.

claim: Flies often encounter olfactory stimuli in the form of odor plumes in natural environments.
source: In natural environments, flies often encounter olfactory stimuli in the form of odor plumes (Murlis et al., 1992), in which the stimulus reaches the antenna intermittently.
evidence: This is established knowledge about natural olfactory stimuli, supported by citation.

claim: ab3A responded robustly to each of the repeated odor pulses in the mutant lacking all four Obps.
source: Consistent with results using a single pulse, ab3A responded robustly to each of the repeated odor pulses in the mutant (Figure 3A,C).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 3A,C.

claim: The dynamics of the ab3A response throughout the entire stimulus period appeared comparable to that of the control.
source: Moreover, the dynamics of the response throughout the entire stimulus period appeared comparable to that of the control.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, based on analysis of data in Figure 3.

claim: The ab3A response to 2-pentanone shows faster adaptation than the response to ethyl hexanoate in control flies.
source: We also tested ab3A with 2-pentanone, which in control flies elicits a strong response with different dynamics: the ab3A response to 2-pentanone shows faster adaptation than the response to ethyl hexanoate.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The response of the mutant ab3A to 2-pentanone was comparable to the control.
source: The response of the mutant to 2-pentanone was again comparable to the control (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: ab3B showed robust responses to repeated pulses of 2-heptanone.
source: The other neuron in the ab3 sensillum, ab3B, also showed robust responses to repeated pulses of an odorant, 2-heptanone. The response dynamics again appeared similar to the control (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 3E.

claim: The response of mutant ab3 to a 5 s pulse of ethyl hexanoate or 2-heptanone was very similar to that of control during the rising phase, peak period, and falling phase.
source: We delivered a 5 s pulse of ethyl hexanoate or 2-heptanone and measured the instantaneous spike rate (Figure 3B,D,F). The response of the mutant was very similar to that of control during the rising phase, during the peak period, and during the falling phase.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 3B,D,F.

claim: ORNs are able to respond comparably to controls when tested with both intermittent and prolonged odor stimuli in the absence of their four abundant Obps.
source: In summary, these ORNs are able to respond comparably to controls when tested with both intermittent and prolonged odor stimuli in the absence of their four abundant Obps.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figure 3.

claim: The ab4A neuron and its receptor Or7a are broadly tuned and respond strongly to a wide variety of short chain aldehydes and alcohols.
source: The ab4A neuron and its receptor Or7a are broadly tuned and respond strongly to a wide variety of short chain aldehydes and alcohols (Hallem and Carlson, 2006; Münch and Galizia, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The ab4A neuron and receptor Or7a have been shown to drive an oviposition preference behavior.
source: This neuron and receptor have been shown to drive an oviposition preference behavior (Lin et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: ab4A has been reported to respond to samples of several long chain compounds that are very hydrophobic, including linoleic acid, (Z)−9-tricosene and bombykol.
source: ab4A has also been reported to respond to samples of several long chain compounds that are very hydrophobic, including linoleic acid (Hallem and Carlson, 2006), (Z)−9-tricosene (Lin et al., 2015) and bombykol (Syed et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: A linoleic acid sample elicited a stronger response from the mutant ab4 sensillum than from a control sensillum.
source: We found that the linoleic acid sample elicited a stronger response from the mutant ab4 sensillum than from a control sensillum (Figure 4A), reminiscent of the greater responses we observed previously with some odorants in the mutant ab8 sensillum (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 4A.

claim: The greater response to linoleic acid in ab4 mutant is observed across a broad range of dilutions of the odor.
source: The greater response is observed across a broad range of dilutions of the odor (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 4A.

claim: Control flies showed a preference for laying eggs on low concentrations of linoleic acid sample, which gradually increased with increasing concentration, but became aversive at the highest concentrations.
source: Control flies showed a preference for laying eggs on low concentrations of the odor, as opposed to agarose without odor, a preference that gradually increased with increasing concentration, but which became aversive at the highest concentrations (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 4C.

claim: The Obp mutant flies showed a preference for linoleic acid sample at low odor concentrations, but with a lower threshold than the control flies.
source: The Obp mutant flies also showed a preference at low odor concentrations, but with a lower threshold than the control flies: the mutant showed a response to lower concentrations than the control.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 4C.

claim: Lower concentrations of linoleic acid sample elicited aversion from the mutant than the control.
source: Likewise, lower concentrations elicited aversion from the mutant than the control.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, supported by data in Figure 4C.

claim: The entire dose-response relationship for linoleic acid sample is shifted in the mutant.
source: The entire dose-response relationship is shifted in the mutant.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figure 4C.

claim: Loss of Obps from ab4 can increase olfactory and oviposition responses.
source: These results show that loss of Obps from ab4 can increase olfactory and oviposition responses.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figure 4.

claim: Evidence became available that the physiological responses of ab4A to long chain hydrophobic compounds may arise from trace impurities in commercial preparations of these compounds.
source: We note that we have referred to the olfactory stimulus as a sample of linoleic acid, rather than linoleic acid per se. After our experiments were conducted, evidence became available that the physiological responses of ab4A to long chain hydrophobic compounds may arise from trace impurities in commercial preparations of these compounds (Schorkopf et al., 2018).
evidence: This is information from another study, supported by citation.

claim: In the ab4 sensillum, Obps can modulate the olfactory response, and in their absence a greater physiological response drives a stronger behavioral response.
source: Taken together, the simplest interpretation of our results is that in the ab4 sensillum, Obps can modulate the olfactory response, and in their absence a greater physiological response of the ab4 sensillum drives a stronger behavioral response.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figure 4.

claim: From the perspective of olfactory sensilla, all of the six tested types of basiconic sensilla responded robustly to all tested odorants despite removal of their abundant Obps.
source: From the perspective of olfactory sensilla, all of the six tested types of basiconic sensilla responded robustly to all tested odorants despite removal of their abundant Obps.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: In no case was an olfactory response diminished by the absence of abundant Obps.
source: In no case was an olfactory response diminished by the absence of these Obps.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: From the perspective of Obps, none was essential for the production of a robust olfactory response.
source: From the perspective of Obps, none was essential for the production of a robust olfactory response.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: In no case did a response decrease for lack of an individual Obp.
source: In no case did a response decrease for lack of an individual Obp.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Obp83a shows only 21.3% identity to Obp28a and 15.6% sequence identity to Obp19a.
source: These Obps are highly divergent, for example Obp83a shows only 21.3% identity to Obp28a and 15.6% sequence identity to Obp19a.
evidence: This is a statement about sequence identity, likely based on sequence analysis.

claim: The analysis included 37 odorants of diverse structures, and 85 odorant-ORN combinations.
source: Our analysis included 37 odorants of diverse structures, and 85 odorant-ORN combinations.
evidence: This describes the scope of the current study.

claim: Four of the odorants tested are more hydrophobic (logP values ranging from 3.85 to 4.28) than the most hydrophobic odorant tested in the previous study, 1-octanol (logP = 3.07).
source: Four of the odorants are more hydrophobic (logP values ranging from 3.85 to 4.28) than the most hydrophobic odorant tested in our previous study, 1-octanol (logP = 3.07), arguing against the possibility that Obps might be essential to transport more hydrophobic odorants through the aqueous sensillar lymph.
evidence: This is a comparison of odorant properties tested in the current vs. previous study.

claim: Responses to olfactory stimuli of diverse temporal structures were robust in the absence of Obps.
source: Responses to olfactory stimuli of diverse temporal structures were also robust.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figure 3.

claim: Loss of Obp19a and Obp28a from ab4 caused an increase in physiological response to an odor stimulus.
source: In the case of the ab4 sensillum, loss of its Obps, that is Obp19a and Obp28a, caused an increase in physiological response to an odor stimulus.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, based on data in Figure 4A.

claim: The increase in physiological response in ab4 mutant is accompanied by an increase in oviposition response.
source: Here we have extended the analysis to the behavioral level, and found that the increase in physiological response is accompanied by an increase in oviposition response.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, based on data in Figure 4C.

claim: All of the data in this study were collected after the mutations had been backcrossed to the control stock for five generations and combined with each other.
source: We note some formal possibilities. First, all of the data in this study were collected after the mutations had been backcrossed to the control stock for five generations and combined with each other.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: It is conceivable that the loss of each Obp initially led to a reduction in olfactory response, but that this phenotype was quickly suppressed during the several generations of genetic crosses.
source: It is conceivable that the loss of each Obp initially led to a reduction in olfactory response, but that this phenotype was quickly suppressed during the several generations of genetic crosses that ensued.
evidence: This is a formal possibility acknowledged by the authors.

claim: If suppression of phenotype occurred, it must have been complete, as opposed to partial, and must have occurred in all sensilla, in all mutants tested, during a limited number of generations.
source: In principle, suppression of nearly any phenotype can occur in Drosophila genetics; in the present case, if such suppression occurred it must have been complete, as opposed to partial, and must have occurred in all sensilla, in all mutants tested, during a limited number of generations, a constellation of requirements that collectively seem unlikely.
evidence: This is a logical argument against the suppression hypothesis.

claim: It is formally possible that the Obps eliminated are redundant in function with other Obps that are expressed at dramatically lower levels.
source: Second, it is formally possible that the Obps we have eliminated are redundant in function with other Obps that are expressed at dramatically lower levels.
evidence: This is a formal possibility acknowledged by the authors.

claim: There are a number of antennal Obp RNAs that are expressed at much lower levels--two or three orders of magnitude lower in nearly all cases--than those of Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b.
source: There are a number of antennal Obp RNAs that are expressed at much lower levels--two or three orders of magnitude lower in nearly all cases--than those of Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b.
evidence: This is based on RNA-seq data from previous work.

claim: The analysis is not exhaustive.
source: Third, we acknowledge that our analysis is not exhaustive.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of study limitations.

claim: A wide diversity of odorants and 12 different ORNs were tested, but for any particular odorant-ORN combination at most three concentrations were tested.
source: We have tested a wide diversity of odorants, and 12 different ORNs, but for any particular odorant-ORN combination we have tested at most three concentrations.
evidence: This describes the scope and limitations of the study.

claim: It is possible that a full dose-response analysis of all odorants would identify a concentration of one at which an Obp mutant showed a reduced response.
source: Although we have tested stimuli that elicit a wide range of ORN activity, it is possible that a full dose-response analysis of all odorants would identify a concentration of one at which an Obp mutant showed a reduced response.
evidence: This is a speculation about what more extensive testing might reveal.

claim: It is possible that shorter or longer pulses of odorants might reveal a strong phenotype.
source: Also, we have not analyzed the response dynamics extensively; in particular it is possible that shorter or longer pulses of odorants might reveal a strong phenotype.
evidence: This is a speculation about what different experimental conditions might reveal.

claim: The interpretation that Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b are not essential for the transport of all odorants in all sensilla is consistent with the results of some other recent studies.
source: The interpretation that Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b are not essential for the transport of all odorants in all sensilla is consistent with the results of some other recent studies.
evidence: This is a statement about consistency with other research.

claim: Obp28a and its tsetse ortholog were found to play a role outside the olfactory system, in hematopoiesis and wound-healing.
source: First, Obp28a and its tsetse ortholog were found to play a role outside the olfactory system, in hematopoiesis and wound-healing (Benoit et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a finding from another study, supported by citation.

claim: Obp59a was discovered to act in humidity detection.
source: Second, another abundant antennal Obp, Obp59a, was discovered to act in humidity detection (Sun et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is a finding from another study, supported by citation.

claim: Many other Obp genes of Drosophila or other insects are expressed outside the olfactory system.
source: Many other Obp genes of Drosophila or other insects are expressed outside the olfactory system (Arya et al., 2010; Galindo and Smith, 2001; Jeong et al., 2013; Li et al., 2005; Matsuo et al., 2007; Shanbhag et al., 2001), again consistent with diverse roles for this large gene family.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Genomic analysis has revealed dramatic expansions of odorant receptor gene families in some insect species, including a variety of Hymenopterans.
source: We note further that genomic analysis has revealed dramatic expansions of odorant receptor gene families in some insect species, including a variety of Hymenopterans (Missbach et al., 2014; Robertson, 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In many cases the expansion of odorant receptor genes is not accompanied by a concomitant expansion of Obps.
source: In many cases this expansion is not accompanied by a concomitant expansion of Obps (Vieira and Rozas, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Camponotus floridanus contains 407 Ors but only 13 Obps.
source: For example, the eusocial ants Camponotus floridanus and Pogonomyrmex barbatus contain 407 and 399 Ors, respectively (Bonasio et al., 2010; Zhou et al., 2012), but only 13 and 16 Obps (McKenzie et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Pogonomyrmex barbatus contains 399 Ors but only 16 Obps.
source: For example, the eusocial ants Camponotus floridanus and Pogonomyrmex barbatus contain 407 and 399 Ors, respectively (Bonasio et al., 2010; Zhou et al., 2012), but only 13 and 16 Obps (McKenzie et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Major imbalances between Or and Obp numbers argue against some classic models of odorant-Obp-receptor interactions.
source: These major imbalances argue against some classic models of odorant-Obp-receptor interactions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the genomic data about Or and Obp numbers.

claim: Removal of Obp28a from ab8 produced greater responses to pulses of some but not all odorants.
source: In our previous study of the ab8 sensillum, we found that removal of Obp28a, its sole abundant Obp, produced greater responses to pulses of some but not all odorants, which we suggested might reflect a role for Obps in a form of molecular gain control (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous work, supported by citation.

claim: The authors suggested that Obps might play a role in a form of molecular gain control.
source: In our previous study of the ab8 sensillum, we found that removal of Obp28a, its sole abundant Obp, produced greater responses to pulses of some but not all odorants, which we suggested might reflect a role for Obps in a form of molecular gain control (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their previous findings.

claim: The present results with the mutant ab4 sensillum revealed an increase in response to several concentrations of one stimulus, but not other odorants.
source: Consistent with these previous findings, the present results with the mutant ab4 sensillum also revealed an increase in response to several concentrations of one stimulus, but not other odorants.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study, based on data in Figure 4.

claim: This study examined basiconic sensilla because the authors have a detailed Obp-to-sensillum map of them.
source: In this study we have examined basiconic sensilla because we have a detailed Obp-to-sensillum map of them.
evidence: This explains the rationale for the study design.

claim: A recent study of trichoid sensilla and intermediate sensilla found that when Obp83a and Obp83b were deleted, responses to all tested odorants were robust.
source: A recent study of other kinds of antennal sensilla, trichoid sensilla and intermediate sensilla, also found that when Obp83a and Obp83b were deleted, responses to all tested odorants were robust (Scheuermann and Smith, 2019).
evidence: This is a finding from another study, supported by citation.

claim: In the Scheuermann and Smith study, the responses of three of ten tested neurons showed slow deactivation kinetics.
source: In this study, however, the responses of three of ten tested neurons showed slow deactivation kinetics; one neuron was tested with two odorants and showed the deactivation phenotype with one odorant but not the other.
evidence: This is a finding from another study, supported by citation.

claim: Scheuermann and Smith propose that after the affected odorants bind and activate receptors, the Obps then remove them.
source: Scheuermann and Smith (2019) propose that after the affected odorants bind and activate receptors, the Obps then remove them.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from another study, supported by citation.

claim: The phenotypes found with the linoleic acid sample are consistent with a model in which these Obps bind an odorant and reduce the concentration that reaches the ORN.
source: The phenotypes we have found with the linoleic acid sample are consistent with a model in which these Obps bind an odorant and reduce the concentration that reaches the ORN.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors based on their findings.

claim: What is most surprising from both studies is that the genetic removal of such abundant proteins does not have more widespread effects on odorant response.
source: However, what is perhaps most surprising from both of these studies is that the genetic removal of such abundant proteins, whose synthesis is likely to incur a major metabolic cost, does not have more widespread effects on odorant response.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings from both studies.

claim: The behavioral effect observed with the linoleic sample is consistent with the physiological effect and may have a great deal of significance for the animal in a natural context.
source: The behavioral effect we observe with the linoleic sample is consistent with the physiological effect and may have a great deal of significance for the animal in a natural context.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings and speculation about their significance.

claim: Loss of Obps does not impair the ability of many sensilla to respond robustly to many odorants.
source: However, it seems clear that loss of Obps does not impair the ability of many sensilla to respond robustly to many odorants.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study.

claim: Some of these antennal Obps might play a role in processes other than olfaction, as they do in other organs.
source: The results raise the interesting possibility that some of these antennal Obps might play a role in processes other than olfaction, as they do in other organs.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings and knowledge of Obp functions in other organs.

claim: This study greatly increases the body of evidence that Obps are not universally required for odorant transport in the Drosophila olfactory system.
source: In summary, this study greatly increases the body of evidence that Obps are not universally required for odorant transport in the Drosophila olfactory system.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study.

claim: The results extend the previous analysis from one to seven basiconic sensilla, from one to four Obps, and from 12 to 37 odorants.
source: Our results extend our previous analysis from one to seven basiconic sensilla, from one to four Obps, and from 12 to 37 odorants, including several more hydrophobic than any tested before.
evidence: This describes the scope of the current study compared to previous work.

claim: The results confirm that Obps can in some cases modulate the physiological response to certain olfactory stimuli.
source: The results confirm, however, that Obps can in some cases modulate the physiological response to certain olfactory stimuli, and we show that Obps can modulate a behavioral response as well.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study.

claim: Obps can modulate a behavioral response.
source: The results confirm, however, that Obps can in some cases modulate the physiological response to certain olfactory stimuli, and we show that Obps can modulate a behavioral response as well.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the current study, based on data in Figure 4C.

claim: The Obp19a- mutant was generated using CRISPR-Cas9 with specific guide RNA sequences.
source: The Obp19a- mutant was generated using the guide RNA sequences (5'-GTCTGCGTCGCCATATCCCT; 5'-GCTAGCTTTTATTGATCATC), using the same procedure that was described in Larter et al. (2016) to create Obp28a-.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: The Obp19a deletion removed 91% of the Obp19a coding sequence.
source: The deletion removed 91% of the Obp19a coding sequence.
evidence: This describes the extent of the genetic deletion.

claim: Obp83a and Obp83b are located within 1 kb of each other.
source: Obp83a and Obp83b are located within 1 kb of each other and were deleted together to create a mutation denoted Obp83a-,b-.
evidence: This describes the genomic organization of these genes.

claim: The Obp83a-,b- deletion removed 27% of the Obp83a coding region, including the first two exons and therefore the start codon.
source: The deletion removed 27% of the Obp83a coding region, including the first two exons and therefore the start codon
evidence: This describes the extent of the genetic deletion.

claim: The Obp83a-,b- deletion removed 85% of the Obp83b coding region.
source: the deletion removed 85% of the Obp83b coding region.
evidence: This describes the extent of the genetic deletion.

claim: 3–6 day old female flies were used for single-sensillum recordings.
source: 3–6 day old female flies were used for single-sensillum recordings, as described previously (Dobritsa et al., 2003).
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: Mutant and control flies were tested in parallel in all experiments.
source: Mutant and control flies were tested in parallel in all experiments.
evidence: This describes the experimental design.

claim: In general, 1 or 2 sensilla were tested per animal, and a total of 2 or 3 odor pulses were delivered to an animal.
source: In general, 1 or 2 sensilla were tested per animal, and a total of 2 or 3 odor pulses were delivered to an animal; in no case were more than 3 sensilla tested or 4 odor pulses delivered.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology.

claim: 10 newly eclosed females were cultured with three males in a vial for 5–6 days before oviposition assays.
source: 10 newly eclosed females were cultured with three males in a vial for 5–6 days.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology for oviposition assays.

claim: Females were maintained in the Petri dish for 20–24 hr in a dark room (25°C, 60% humidity) during oviposition assays.
source: Ten females were maintained in the Petri dish for 20–24 hr in a dark room (25°C, 60% humidity).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions for oviposition assays.

claim: A very small fraction of dishes contained fewer than 10 eggs and were excluded from the oviposition assay.
source: A very small fraction of dishes contained fewer than 10 eggs and were excluded from the assay.
evidence: This describes the data exclusion criteria.

claim: Different basiconic sensilla contain different subsets of four abundant Obps: Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a, and Obp83b.
source: Different basiconic sensilla contain different subsets of four abundant Obps: Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a, and Obp83b (Figure 1E) (Larter et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge from the authors' previous work, illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: Obp19a and Obp28a are the two abundant Obps expressed in ab4, ab5 and ab6.
source: We then crossed the deletion mutations to each other so as to create mutants that are lacking the following combinations of Obps: Obp19a and Obp28a, which are the two abundant Obps expressed in ab4, ab5 and ab6
evidence: This is based on the Obp-to-sensillum map from previous work.

claim: Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b are the three Obps expressed in ab1 and ab2.
source: Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b, the three Obps expressed in ab1 and ab2
evidence: This is based on the Obp-to-sensillum map from previous work.

claim: Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b are the four Obps expressed in ab3.
source: and Obp19a, Obp28a, Obp83a and Obp83b, the four Obps expressed in ab3.
evidence: This is based on the Obp-to-sensillum map from previous work.

claim: On the order of 1000 basiconic sensilla were examined from the antennae of ~20 mutant flies lacking all four Obps.
source: On the order of 1000 basiconic sensilla were examined from the antennae of ~20 mutant flies lacking all four Obps.
evidence: This describes the scope of the morphological examination.

claim: The collection of odorants tested represents a variety of chemical classes, including alcohols, ketones, aldehydes, esters, terpenes and aromatics.
source: The collection of odorants tested in this initial analysis represents a variety of chemical classes, including alcohols, ketones, aldehydes, esters, terpenes and aromatics.
evidence: This describes the diversity of odorants tested.

claim: The hydrophobicity of tested odorants varies over more than five orders of magnitude, ranging from 2,3-butanedione (logP = −1.33) to geranyl acetate (logP = 4.10).
source: Their hydrophobicity varies over more than five orders of magnitude, ranging from 2,3-butanedione (logP = −1.33, where P is the partition coefficient between octanol and water) to geranyl acetate, the most hydrophobic (logP = 4.10)(Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the range of odorant hydrophobicity tested, supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The tested ORNs range from broadly tuned (e.g., ab3A) to narrowly tuned (e.g., ab4B).
source: The tested ORNs range from broadly tuned, for example ab3A, which responds to many odorants (Hallem and Carlson, 2006; Münch and Galizia, 2016), to narrowly tuned, for example ab4B, which responds to geosmin (Stensmyr et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the diversity of ORN tuning, supported by citations.

claim: The control responses to the odor stimuli extended over a broad range, from modest (~20 spikes/s) to very strong (~220 spikes/s).
source: The control responses to the odor stimuli in this experiment also extended over a broad range, from modest (~20 spikes/s) to very strong (~220 spikes/s).
evidence: This describes the range of control responses observed.
